title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Release Date: What Anthropic Has Confirmed
summary: Claude Sonnet 5.5 has no release date yet. Anthropic named it on September 22, 2026, with no price or benchmarks. Here is what is confirmed vs. rumored.
body_markdown:
Anthropic has not given a release date for Claude Sonnet 5.5. The company named the model once, in its September 22, 2026 launch announcement for[Claude Opus 5.5](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-claude-opus-5-5) , and said only that Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 would follow "in the coming weeks." As of September 28, 2026, there is no published date, no price, no benchmark scores, and no model card. Anthropic's model documentation still lists Claude Sonnet 5 as the current Sonnet.


Everything beyond that single announcement is unverified. A cluster of leaks and social media posts has floated a late-September or early-October window, along with a list of specifications. None of it comes from Anthropic, and much of it restates numbers that already belong to Sonnet 5.


## Anthropic has confirmed the model, not the date


The confirmed record on Claude Sonnet 5.5 fits in two sentences. Anthropic introduced Opus 5.5 on September 22 as the first model in a new Claude 5.5 family. In the same announcement, it said Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 would arrive in the coming weeks with many of the same improvements to performance, efficiency, and safety.


Anthropic product lead Mike Krieger repeated the point on X, using the same "coming weeks" phrasing. That is the extent of the official word.


Two things follow from it. The model is real by Anthropic's own confirmation, so this is not a case of a rumored product that may never ship. But "coming weeks," said on September 22, is a direction, not a date. It is consistent with an October launch without committing to one.


## The rumored release dates come from leaks, not Anthropic


Every specific date circulating for Claude Sonnet 5.5 traces back to social media posts and one outlet repeating them. Reports have named September 30 or October 1 as a likely window, tied to claims that partners received short access windows and that the model is in limited testing.


These dates should be treated as speculation. Anthropic has not confirmed any of them, and no independent source has verified the partner-testing claims. The reporting that named the window said as much directly, framing it as a rumor with a plausible basis rather than a schedule.


One recurring theory ties the timing to OpenAI's DevDay on September 30, positioning Sonnet 5.5 against[GPT-6 Sol](https://emergent.sh/learn/gpt-6-sol-benchmarks) . The argument is that Anthropic would ship Sonnet 5.5 the same week for competitive cover. That is a narrative, not evidence. Registry leaks and codenames have surfaced weeks ahead of past Claude launches, so proximity to a rival event proves nothing about the actual ship date.


## The leaked specs are mostly Claude Sonnet 5's current numbers


The most important thing to know about the leaked Sonnet 5.5 specifications is that most of them already describe Sonnet 5. Circulating claims give the model a 1 million-token context window, a 128,000-token maximum output, and pricing of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cache reads at $0.20 per million.


Each of those figures is already published for[Claude Sonnet 5](https://emergent.sh/learn/what-is-claude-sonnet-5) . Anthropic made the $2 and $10 pricing permanent in August 2026 rather than moving to a higher rate. So a leak that Sonnet 5.5 will keep these terms is really a prediction that nothing changes, which tells buyers little they did not already know.


*Claude Sonnet 5.5 leaked specifications compared to Claude Sonnet 5, as of September 2026*


Specification Claude Sonnet 5 (published) Claude Sonnet 5.5 (rumored)


Context window 1M tokens Rumored 1M, unconfirmed


Maximum output 128K tokens Rumored 128K, unconfirmed


Input price $2 per million tokens Rumored $2, unconfirmed


Output price $10 per million tokens Rumored $10, unconfirmed


Cache reads $0.20 per million tokens Rumored $0.20, unconfirmed


Release Available since June 2026 "Coming weeks" (official), late Sept to Oct (rumor)


One newer leak breaks from the pattern and, in doing so, undercuts the rest. A September 28 report cited an unverified claim that Sonnet 5.5 carries an 872,000-token context window rather than 1 million. That figure contradicts the earlier 1 million-token claim. Two conflicting numbers from the same rumor mill are a reminder that no capacity, price, or availability detail is settled until Anthropic publishes documentation.


## A model registry entry is the strongest signal, and it is still not a launch


The most concrete leak is a model identifier, not a benchmark. A developer flagged that the string claude-sonnet-5-5 appears in the model registry of a third-party coding client, wired behind a feature flag, while that client's public model list still stops at Sonnet 5.


That is more substantial than a screenshot of a chat window, because client registries are where vendors place real endpoint names before a public launch. It suggests a launch is close. It is still not a release. There is no pricing, no context-window confirmation, and no safety documentation attached to it, and the account that surfaced it is a leak account rather than Anthropic.


The practical takeaway for anyone building on Claude is simple: keep production traffic on the documented Sonnet 5 identifier. Pointing a live workflow at an unannounced model string because a screenshot uses it is a poor basis for a production decision.


## What to watch for when Sonnet 5.5 actually ships


The real confirmation will be Anthropic's own model page, not another leak. When Sonnet 5.5 launches, Anthropic will publish an official model ID, a pricing table, benchmark results, and a system card. Until those exist, the release date remains open.


Two details will matter most on launch day. The first is efficiency, since Anthropic tied the whole 5.5 family to the same story that defined[Opus 5.5 pricing](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-opus-5-5-pricing) : doing equivalent work with fewer tokens. The second is the tokenizer, because Sonnet 5 introduced one that produces more tokens for the same text, which means a lower per-token price does not always translate into a lower bill. Anyone planning to migrate should recount representative prompts rather than assume the numbers carry over.
